extracted.intended_audience: State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Registration Agencies, apprenticeship program sponsors, Office of Apprenticeship staff, and legal/regulatory stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing State Apprenticeship Agency recognition, reporting, program review, EEO obligations, recordkeeping, enforcement, appeals, and related procedures for sponsors and Registration Agencies under the Department of Labor apprenticeship regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional recognition of an SAA for registered CTE apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: An SAA seeking recognition to serve as a Registration Agency for registered CTE apprenticeship must submit the following elements:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) The State's proposed or current registered CTE apprenticeship laws as described in § 29.24(g)(8). (ii) A written agreement between the State entity seeking recognition and the State's CTE Agency as described in § 29.24(a)(2). (iii) A narrative summary of the State's strategic vision and strategy for expanding registered CTE apprenticeship programs under subpart B of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which OA will convey full recognition for Federal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full recognition if the Administrator has determined: (i) The State's apprenticeship laws meet or exceed the minimum standards as described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section. (ii) The State's Plan includes all strategic planning elements that are complete and responsive to the requirements in paragraph (b)(2). (iii) The State's Plan includes all operational elements that are complete and responsive to the requirements in paragraph (b)(3). (iv) The State's Plan includes all of the assurances as required in paragraph (b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for provisional recognition and its limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional recognition if Administrator determines the State's apprenticeship laws meet minimum standards and State's Plan includes required assurances, but strategic planning elements or operational elements are incomplete or nonresponsive; deficiencies must be resolvable with OA technical assistance and an approved corrective action plan. A State may be provisionally recognized for no more than one full planning cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Administrator will deny recognition for Federal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial of recognition if: (i) The State's apprenticeship laws do not meet the minimum standards described in paragraph (b)(1); or (ii) The SAA is unable to be fully approved within one full planning cycle after having been provisionally recognized, as described in paragraph (c)(2). Procedures for such denial are described in § 29.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA retention of registration authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances where the Office of Apprenticeship retains authority to register programs/apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding SAA recognition, the Administrator will retain authority to register apprenticeship programs and apprentices on both a local and nationwide basis for Federal purposes when the Administrator determines a sponsor seeking registration has satisfied the requirements described in this part and where such action would further the interests of the National Apprenticeship System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic monitoring and review of SAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: OA will monitor and review SAA compliance to ensure consistency with approved State Apprenticeship Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA will monitor and review the compliance of an SAA, in instances where the Administrator determines such a review is warranted, to ensure it is operating consistent with its approved State Apprenticeship Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derecognition of SAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator may derecognize an SAA for failure to operate consistent with its approved plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may derecognize an SAA with full or provisional recognition when the Administrator determines that the SAA is not operating consistent with its approved State Apprenticeship Plan. The processes and procedures for such derecognition are described in § 29.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of provisionally approved SAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds and mechanics for suspending a provisionally approved SAA's authority to register new programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may suspend the authority of a provisionally approved SAA to register new apprenticeship programs for failure to submit, and receive OA's approval of, a corrective action plan as required in paragraph (c)(2). OA will provide written notice; suspension takes effect 30 calendar days after notice and ends upon the State's submission of a corrective action plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of State activities without recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on conducting certain State activities when SAA lacks recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OA denies a State Apprenticeship Plan or derecognizes an SAA, the State must not conduct the activities specified in § 29.26(a) until OA conveys full or provisional recognition as described in § 29.27(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA reporting obligations: data collection and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs' requirements to collect and report sponsor information to OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAAs are required to collect the information from sponsors described in § 29.25(a) and (b). On at least a quarterly basis, SAAs must report the information collected from sponsors described in paragraphs (a) and (b)(1) of § 29.25 to OA. On an annual basis, the SAA will report the information collected under § 29.25(b)(2) to the Administrator. The Administrator will make the information described publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting systems and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted systems for meeting reporting requirements and minimum security expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAAs may meet reporting requirements by either: (1) Utilizing a Department-provided case management system; or (2) Maintaining a State system capable of reporting individual apprentice record level information to OA in a manner prescribed by the Administrator, and that meets minimum security requirements prescribed by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial/derecognition process: notice content and remediation timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: What written notice from the Administrator must include and the remedy timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Administrator denies a State Apprenticeship Plan or derecognizes an SAA, the Administrator will issue a written notice that includes: (i) The reason(s) for the denial or derecognition; (ii) The needed remedial measure(s); and (iii) The timeframe for addressing those measures, which will be no longer than 12 months from the date of the written notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to hearing and adjudicative procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline and procedures for requesting and conducting hearings after final determination, and standards of review and appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If State fails remedial measures, Administrator may issue a final determination stating State may request a hearing with OALJ within 30 calendar days. Requests for hearing must be sent to OALJ within 30 days with copy to Administrator. Administrator will transmit the administrative file to OALJ. Procedures in part 18 apply except technical rules of evidence will not apply; ALJ may exclude irrelevant evidence, authorize discovery, and must issue a written decision within 90 calendar days of close of the hearing record. ALJ must uphold Administrator unless sponsor shows decision was arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law. Decision constitutes final agency action unless petition for review filed with ARB within 15 calendar days; ARB may accept case within 30 days and must issue decision within 180 calendar days of close of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary withdrawal of recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: SAA may voluntarily withdraw recognition and the process thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SAA may request voluntary withdrawal from its recognition status at any time. The Administrator will derecognize the SAA after the State sends a formal notice of withdrawal to the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator actions after derecognition: sponsor notification and transitional registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps OA will take after derecognition and how sponsors may seek registration with OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Notify sponsors in the State and effect public notice. (2) Notify sponsors that 45 calendar days after determination Department will cease to recognize for Federal purposes each apprenticeship program previously registered with the SAA unless within that time the sponsor submits an application for registration with OA. (i) Within 90 days of receiving the application, OA will review application to determine if it meets registration requirements in § 29.10(a). (ii) OA will approve an application in accordance with procedures in § 29.10(b). (iii) OA will deny applications that do not meet § 29.10(b) and procedures in § 29.10(c) apply to declined applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State obligations after derecognition
rubrics_metrics.description: State duties to transfer records, notify sponsors/apprentices, and cooperate during transition after derecognition or withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Provide all apprenticeship program standards, apprenticeship agreements, completion records, cancellation and suspension records, EEO compliance review files, and any other documents relating to the State's registered apprenticeship programs to the Department. (2) Within 15 calendar days of receiving a final determination, unless State requests a hearing, advise all sponsors that federal benefits of registration are no longer available to apprentices as of 45 calendar days after the Administrator's final determination; communications must direct apprentices to OA for potential transfer. (3) Cooperate fully with the Administrator during a transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Participation and privacy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to issue Certificates and requirement to follow privacy laws in disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator or recognized SAA may provide a Certificate of Participation to demonstrate a program sponsor's or participating employer's compliance with any Federal purpose or State benefit associated with participation in a registered apprenticeship program. Disclosure of information in accordance with this section must comply with applicable Federal or State information and privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of equal opportunity pledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors' obligation to publish the EEO pledge in standards and public materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sponsor must publish its equal opportunity pledge—set forth in paragraph (c) of § 30.3—in the standards of apprenticeship required under part 29 and in appropriate publications such as apprentice and employee handbooks, policy manuals, newsletters, or other documents disseminated by the sponsor that describe the nature of the sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization analysis schedule (race, sex, ethnicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: When sponsors must conduct apprenticeship program workforce analyses and how to use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sponsor is required to conduct an apprenticeship program workforce analysis at each program review, and again if and when 3 years have passed without a program review. This updated workforce analysis should be compared to the utilization goal established at the sponsor's most recent program review to determine if the sponsor is underutilized, according to the process in § 30.5(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability analyses at program review
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must work with Registration Agency to conduct availability analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors, working with the Registration Agency, will conduct availability analyses at each program review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization goals for individuals with disabilities: schedule of evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency and grouping requirements for workforce analysis relative to individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sponsor must conduct its apprentice workforce analysis at each program review, and again if and when 3 years have passed without a program review. This updated workforce analysis, grouped according to major occupation group, should then be compared to the utilization goal established under § 30.7(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of apprentices: inclusion in written standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor selection procedures must be included in the written standards submitted for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sponsor's procedures for selection of apprentices must be included in the written plan for standards of apprenticeship submitted to and approved by the Registration Agency, as required under part 29 of this title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: operational and personnel information
rubrics_metrics.description: Records sponsors must maintain relevant to program operations and EEO complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information relative to the operation of the apprenticeship program, including but not limited to job assignments in all components of the occupation as required under part 29, promotion, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, rates of pay, other forms of compensation, conditions of work, hours of work, hours of training provided, and any other personnel records relevant to EEO complaints filed with the Registration Agency under § 30.14 or with other enforcement agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to records for program reviews and investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must permit inspection and copying of records and provide access in specified manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sponsor must permit access during normal business hours to its places of business for on-site program reviews and complaint investigations and allow inspection and copying of books, accounts, and records, including electronic records, and any other material the Registration Agency deems relevant. Sponsor must also provide off-site access for reviews and investigations, and upon request provide information about all formats, including specific electronic formats, in which its records are available. Information obtained will be used only in connection with administration of this part or other applicable EEO laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews: conduct and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: How Registration Agencies will conduct program reviews and what they may include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registration Agency will regularly conduct program reviews to determine if the sponsor maintains compliance with the EEO requirements, and will also conduct such reviews when circumstances so warrant. A program review may consist of comprehensive analyses and evaluations through off-site reviews (desk audits of records) and on-site reviews at the sponsor's establishment that may involve examination of records required under this part; inspection and copying of documents related to recordkeeping; and interviews with employees, apprentices, journeyworkers, supervisors, managers, and hiring officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of program review findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline and form of notice Registration Agency must provide after completing a program review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 45 days of completing a program review, the Registration Agency must present a written Notice of Program Review Findings to the sponsor's contact person through registered or certified mail, with return receipt requested. If the program review indicates a failure to comply, the Notice will inform the sponsor and set forth required information (e.g., specific violations and required remedial actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance response to Notice of Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors' required response options and timing after receiving a Notice indicating failure to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sponsor receives a Notice of Program Review Findings that indicates a failure to comply, the sponsor must, within 45 days of notification, either implement a compliance action plan and notify the Registration Agency of that plan or submit a written rebuttal to the Findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints: thorough investigation and case record
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency's obligations in investigating complaints and constructing the case record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency must complete a thorough investigation of the allegations and develop a complete case record that must contain at least the name, address, and telephone number of each person interviewed, the interview statements, copies, transcripts, or summaries of pertinent documents where appropriate, and a narrative report of the investigation with references to exhibits and other evidence related to the alleged violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints: notification of findings and complainant protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of investigation results and protection of complainant identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency must provide written notification of the Registration Agency's findings to both the respondent and the complainant; and must protect the identity of the complainant to the extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement actions and suspension of registration rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency's enforcement powers and suspension/deregistration process for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Registration Agency determines sponsor is not operating in accordance with this part, it must notify sponsor in writing of specific violation(s) and may take enforcement actions. Specifically, the Registration Agency may suspend the sponsor's right to register new apprentices if sponsor fails to implement a compliance action plan to correct violations within 45 days of notification (or within 45 days of Registration Agency upholding initial findings). If compliance plan is not implemented within 45 days of suspension notification, the Registration Agency may institute proceedings to deregister the program in accordance with deregistration proceedings in part 29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against intimidation and retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on retaliatory actions against persons who participate in investigations or reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is prohibited to retaliate against individuals who furnished information to, or assisted or participated in any manner in, any investigation, program review, proceeding, or hearing under this part or any Federal or State equal opportunity law.

rubrics_metrics.name: State EEO plan submission and Administrator concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: SAA obligations to submit State EEO plan and obtain Administrator concurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 1 year of January 18, 2017 (unless extension granted), an SAA seeking to obtain or maintain recognition must submit to OA a State EEO plan. An SAA seeking to obtain or maintain recognition must obtain the Administrator's written concurrence in any proposed State EEO plan, as well as any subsequent modification to that plan, as provided in part 29.

rubrics_metrics.name: State EEO plan nonconformity and rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences if a State fails to address nonconformities in its State EEO plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State does not submit a revised State EEO plan that addresses identified nonconformities within 90 days from the date OA provides the SAA with written notification of areas of nonconformity, OA will begin the process set forth in part 29 to rescind recognition of the SAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recordkeeping retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Record retention requirement for recognized State Apprenticeship Agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recognized SAA must keep all records pertaining to program reviews, complaint investigations, and any other records pertinent to a determination of compliance with this part. These records must be maintained for 5 years from the date of their creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA retained authorities regarding program reviews and deregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific authorities OA retains even when SAAs are recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA retains the full authority to: (1) Conduct program reviews of all registered apprenticeship programs; (2) Deregister for Federal purposes an apprenticeship program registered with a recognized SAA as provided in part 29; and other authorities as provided in part 29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: How invalidation of any provision by a court will be handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should a court hold any portion of any provision(s) of this part to be invalid, the provision will be construed so as to continue to give the maximum effect permitted by law; if held totally invalid or unenforceable, the provision or subprovision will be severable and will not affect the remainder of this part.
